sections.heading: Area between a curve and the x-axis

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by $y=4-x^2$ and the $x$-axis.

questions.answer: Intersect: $x^2=x+2 \Rightarrow x^2-x-2=0 \Rightarrow (x-2)(x+1)=0$: $x=-1,2$. On this interval $x+2 \geq x^2$. Area $=\int_{-1}^{2}\left[(x+2)-x^2\right]dx=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}+2x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{2}=\left(2+4-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-2+\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{10}{3}-\left(-\frac{7}{6}\right)=\frac{9}{2}$.

questions.q: Find the area between $y=\sqrt{x}$ and $y=x^2$ on $[0,1]$.
Find the area of the region bounded by $x=y^2$ and $x=y+2$, integrating with respect to $y$.
questions.answer: Intersect: $y^2=y+2 \Rightarrow y^2-y-2=0 \Rightarrow (y-2)(y+1)=0$: $y=-1,2$. On this interval $y+2\geq y^2$. Area $=\int_{-1}^{2}\left[(y+2)-y^2\right]dy=\left[\frac{y^2}{2}+2y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{2}=\left(2+4-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-2+\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{9}{2}$.

questions.q: Find the total area between $y=\sin x$ and $y=\cos x$ on $[0,\pi]$, accounting for the curves crossing at $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
questions.answer: On $[0,\frac{\pi}{4}]$, $\cos x\geq\sin x$; on $[\frac{\pi}{4},\pi]$, $\sin x\geq\cos x$. Total area $=\int_0^{\pi/4}(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx+\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi}(\sin x-\cos x)\,dx$. First: $[\sin x+\cos x]_0^{\pi/4}=\sqrt{2}-1$. Second: $[-\cos x-\sin x]_{\pi/4}^{\pi}=(1-0)-(-\sqrt{2})=1+\sqrt{2}$. Total $=(\sqrt{2}-1)+(1+\sqrt{2})=2\sqrt{2}\approx2.83$.

sections.heading: Area using the more efficient variable of integration

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by $y^2=4-x$ and $x=0$, choosing the more convenient variable of integration.
questions.answer: Solving for $x$: $x=4-y^2$, bounded by $x=0$ (i.e. $y=\pm2$). Integrating with respect to $y$ is easier: Area $=\int_{-2}^{2}(4-y^2)\,dy=\left[4y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2}=\left(8-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(-8+\frac{8}{3}\right)=\frac{16}{3}+\frac{16}{3}=\frac{32}{3}$.

questions.q: Set up (but do not evaluate) the integral expression for the area of the region enclosed by $y=e^x$, $y=\ln x$, and the lines $x=1$ and $x=2$.
questions.answer: On $[1,2]$, $e^x\geq\ln x$ (since $e^x$ grows much faster). Area $=\int_1^2\left(e^x-\ln x\right)dx$.

questions.q: Set up (but do not evaluate) the integral expression for the area between $y=x^3-4x$ and the $x$-axis on $[-2,2]$, accounting for the curve crossing the axis at $x=-2,0,2$.

sections.heading: Area between curves and a table of values

questions.q: Functions $f$ and $g$ satisfy $f(x)\geq g(x)$ for all $x$ in $[0,6]$, with selected values given: $f(0)=10$, $f(2)=8$, $f(4)=9$, $f(6)=12$ and $g(0)=3$, $g(2)=4$, $g(4)=5$, $g(6)=6$. Use the Trapezoidal Rule with these 3 equal subintervals to approximate the area between the curves, $\int_0^6[f(x)-g(x)]\,dx$.
The graph shows $y=x^2$ and $y=x+2$ from an earlier problem, together with the region between them.
questions.answer: The line $y=x+2$ lies above the parabola $y=x^2$ throughout $(-1,2)$, matching the earlier setup $\int_{-1}^{2}\left[(x+2)-x^2\right]dx=\frac{9}{2}$.

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by $y=x^3-x$ and $y=0$ on $[-1,1]$, accounting for the sign change at $x=0$.
questions.answer: On $[-1,0]$, $x^3-x\geq0$; on $[0,1]$, $x^3-x\leq0$. Area $=\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx+\left|\int_0^1(x^3-x)\,dx\right|$. $\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{-1}^0=0-\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{4}$. By symmetry the second piece is also $\frac{1}{4}$. Total area $=\frac{1}{2}$.

sections.heading: Area between an exponential curve and a line

questions.q: Find the area between $y=e^x$ and $y=x+1$ on $[0,2]$ (note $e^x\geq x+1$ for all $x$, tangent only at $x=0$).

Two competing companies' profit rates (in thousands of dollars per year) are $P_1(t)=50-2t$ and $P_2(t)=30+t$ over the first 10 years. Find the total difference in cumulative profit between the two companies over this period, using the area between the curves.
questions.answer: Intersection: $50-2t=30+t \Rightarrow 20=3t \Rightarrow t=\frac{20}{3}\approx6.67$. For $t<\frac{20}{3}$, $P_1>P_2$; for $t>\frac{20}{3}$, $P_2>P_1$. Total absolute difference $=\left|\int_0^{20/3}(P_1-P_2)\,dt\right|+\left|\int_{20/3}^{10}(P_2-P_1)\,dt\right|$, which can be computed piecewise using $P_1-P_2=20-3t$.
